title: Dedicated-to-Hosted Spillover: routing guardrails, region & tier selection, and fallback model variants
creator: Eleanor Park
description:
Goal: Implement a deterministic, policy-driven routing layer that moves requests from Dedicated capacity to Hosted (spillover) only under controlled conditions and with safeguards for latency, cost, and data residency. Scope covers region selection, customer tier routing (prod/paid vs dev/free), and automatic fallback to model variants (quantized/smaller) with observable circuit-breakers and audit trails.

Background: Several enterprise customers want guaranteed Dedicated pool isolation but also want graceful handling when Dedicated capacity is exhausted (e.g., burst or maintenance windows). Current runtime routes to any available pool which can violate data-residency preferences, increase cost unexpectedly, or surface low-quality model outputs. This ticket standardizes routing decisions across the control plane, runtime, and console.

Key design constraints and requirements:
- Respect customer configuration in this priority order: data_residency_tag (region), customer_tier (paid/prod vs dev), model_pin/version, max_allowed_cost_per_token, allowed_fallback_variants.
- Default behavior: no automatic spillover for customers with isolation_enabled=true unless explicit allow_spillover policy present.
- Controlled spillover trigger conditions: Dedicated pool overload > 80% for > 2s OR Dedicated node health degraded AND fallback budget available.
- Region selection: prefer same-region Hosted pool; if unavailable, fallback only to allowed regions in customer policy.
- Tier routing: prod/paid requests must prefer Dedicated; dev/free may route to Hosted by default.
- Fallback model variants: prefer lower-cost quantized variant of same model (e.g., 8-bit), then smaller family (e.g., Llama2-13B -> 7B), with a max quality degradation score (configurable).
- Safeguards: cost cap enforcement, explicit customer opt-in for cross-region spillover, audit log entry for each spillover event, per-request routing trace id, and immediate alerting when spillover rate exceeds threshold (e.g., 0.1% sustained).
- Sticky routing: session affinity for chat conversations where KV cache exists; spillover should try to preserve KV prefixes or invalidate safely.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Routing policy engine evaluates region, tier, and model_pin and returns a deterministic route decision within 2ms median.
2) For a Dedicated-backed customer with isolation_enabled=true, no requests spill to Hosted unless allow_spillover=true and budget remains.
3) When Dedicated is overloaded, requests spill to Hosted only if allowed_regions include fallback region and cost cap not exceeded.
4) Fallback model variants follow ordered preference (quantized -> smaller model) and are recorded in request traces.
5) Console displays spillover metrics per-customer and a detailed audit stream.
6) Unit/integration tests covering edge cases (region blacklists, simultaneous pool flaps, cross-region opt-out).
implementation_notes:
- Add a new policy-eval RPC in control plane (policy-service) returning route action: {route_target, reason_code, fallback_variant, trace_id} (wire format TBD).
- Runtime will consult policy-service with request metadata: customer_id, model_pin, region_hint, tier, session_id, cost_budget.
- Implement a transient circuit-breaker with exponential backoff before allowing repeated spillover to a particular hosted pool.
- Persist spillover decisions to audit-log index (streams/audit/spillovers) and emit metrics: spillover_rate, avg_spill_latency, avg_cost_delta.
- Expose feature flags for gradual rollout: ff.spillover.allow_for_tier.dev, ff.spillover.enable_cross_region.
- Performance: cache policy-service decisions for identical keys for 500ms to reduce latency and load.
- Security: ensure no secret or PII leaks to Hosted pools that violate customer residency; add assertion checks in policy-service.

testing_plan:
- Unit tests for policy evaluation logic (edge permutations of region, tier, pin).
- Integration: allocate simulated Dedicated pool pressure (chaos test) and verify spillover obeys policies.
- Load test: ensure median route decision latency < 2ms with 10k rps and 500ms policy cache.
- Security review: penetration checklist for cross-region data flows.
- Rollout: staged on internal accounts -> beta customers with allow_spillover opt-in -> gradual open to eligible customers.
- QA checklist embedded in GH PR template; link to e2e job: ci/route-spillover-e2e
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Unexpected cost spikes if policy mis-evaluates allowed_fallback_variants. Mitigation: hard cost cap at enforcement gate and canary trials with cost alerts.
Risk: Increased latency for session-affine chats when KV cannot be migrated. Mitigation: prefer quantized same-model variant in same region and fall back to session invalidation flow with graceful user-facing message.
Risk: Regulatory breach from cross-region spillover. Mitigation: strong opt-out default (no cross-region without explicit allow) and automated pre-check that blocks decisions violating data_residency_tag.
